lineas.texto: Zoom into your phone screen, and you won't find a single white pixel.
Every pixel is just three tiny lights. Red, green and blue.
Turn on red and green together, and your brain sees yellow.
All three at full power, and you see white. Every color on your screen is a mix of these three.
But how does it know where your finger is?
Under the glass sits an invisible grid of wires, each one holding a tiny electric charge.
Your finger conducts electricity, so when it touches, it pulls away some of that charge.
The phone checks which row and which column lost charge, over a hundred times a second.
That's why regular gloves don't work. The fabric doesn't conduct, so the grid feels nothing.
